_about: ASSEMBLY.md steps mapped to the GLB's objects (BUILD/guide/build_guide.py). new_objects: objects that first appear in the step, from checks.json assembly_order. focus_objects: what the viewer highlights (new objects, plus a merged bench sub-assembly). Directions are in the design frame: +X right, +Y front, +Z up. status 'flagged' lists the reason in flags.

fields.label: Prints
fields.html: all 9 plates (PRINT_PLAN.md), and the three tools: encoder jig, pocket coupon, 45 deg prop.

fields.label: Measured
fields.html: MEASURE_FIRST.md done, and the model rebuilt if anything changed.

fields.label: Pilots
fields.html: clean every Ø2.5 pilot with a Ø2.5 drill if your printer prints holes small. A screw that has to be forced splits the boss.

fields.label: Servos on the bench, through the controller
fields.html:
• give the pan, tilt and feeder servos different bus IDs (they all ship as ID 1, and after step 11a they share one bus);
  • label each servo with its ID;
  • command each servo to its mid position (500 on Hiwonder's 0..1000 scale) before its horn goes on, and don't turn the output by hand after that. Mid is pan 0, tilt 0 and the feeder's park position. Fine trim is done in firmware at step 15.

fields.label: Tape check
fields.html: the hockey tape is 1 in wide (it is trimmed to 13.8 at step 6f).

warnings.text: All three servos ship as bus ID 1. Give pan, tilt and feeder different IDs and label each servo before anything else: after step 11a they share one bus.
Command each servo to mid (500 on the 0..1000 scale) before its horn goes on, and don't turn the output by hand after that. Mid is pan 0, tilt 0 and the feeder's park position.
Measure first: MEASURE_FIRST.md done and the model rebuilt if anything changed, before the plates that depend on it.
Clean every Ø2.5 pilot with a Ø2.5 drill if your printer prints holes small. A forced screw splits the boss.

steps.title: Base shell upside down; DeWalt adapter

assembly_order.step: 1 base shell upside down: adapter into its fence, M3 x 20 self-tappers from the deck top

tools: 2 mm hex or Phillips to suit the csk heads

fasteners.text: 4 x M3 x 20 countersunk ST.

fields.label: Do
fields.html: lay the base shell deck-down. Put the adapter into its fence, then drive the 4 screws from the deck top into the adapter's corner holes.

fields.label: Check
fields.html: the battery slides on and off the rail by hand. The screw tips sit 4.56 above the battery face (row FST_adapter-BUY_battery), so nothing scrapes the pack.

steps.check: the battery slides on and off the rail by hand. The screw tips sit 4.56 above the battery face (row FST_adapter-BUY_battery), so nothing scrapes the pack.

warnings.text: Measure first (item 6): the adapter's corner hole size is unknown. If the holes are Ø3 or bigger the self-tappers won't bite; use machine screws and nuts, or epoxy. Screw tips must stay 3 or more above the battery face (4.56 now).

fields.label: Check
fields.html: the horn sits flat and centred; the pinion teeth spin true on the spline.

steps.check: the horn sits flat and centred; the pinion teeth spin true on the spline.

warnings.text: Measure first (item 3): check the horn's bolt circle against the dimples before drilling through.

notes: PRT_cable_clip*: Glob matches nothing; the model has no cable clips and ASSEMBLY.md doesn't call for any.
FST_clip_*: Glob matches nothing; no clip screws in the model or in ASSEMBLY.md.

assembly_order.step: 3 floor into the shell, cables; v2-A2-02 launcher base lead (phase + encoder) from the MotorGo to the hub with its U-loop under the hub gear

fasteners.text: 8 x M3 x 12 countersunk ST, from below.
fasteners.spec: M3 x 12 countersunk ST, from below.

fields.label: Do, before the floor closes
fields.html:
• run 12 V (adapter to buck, buck to MotorGo, buck to controller), the UART lead and the USB-C;
  • run the pan bus lead: from the controller up the riser, with its U-loop hanging under the hub gear, and up the pan axis. Leave its plug on, push the plug end up through the hub bore and coil it above the turntable;
  • run the launcher base lead: from the MotorGo J6/J8 phase pads and its encoder connector, through its own U-loop under the hub gear, up to the hand-over point in the hub bore.

fields.label: Check
fields.html:
• both U-loops hang free; they are the ±90 pan slack;
  • turn the turntable to both pan stops: nothing pulls tight or rubs the gears;
  • then fit the floor.

steps.check: - both U-loops hang free; they are the ±90 pan slack; - turn the turntable to both pan stops: nothing pulls tight or rubs the gears; - then fit the floor.

warnings.text: Both U-loops must hang free under the hub gear: they are the ±90 pan slack. Turn the turntable to both stops before the floor closes.

steps.title: Motor into the nacelle; body on

assembly_order.label: 6a
assembly_order.step: 6a pod on the bench: motor into the nacelle bore (crush ribs), body onto the nacelle plate; motor + nacelle screws from inside the guard; phase leads into the journal bore

fasteners.text: 4 x M3 x 10 pan (machine, into the motor face)
fasteners.spec: M3 x 10 pan (machine, into the motor face)

fasteners.spec: M3 x 12 pan ST (nacelle to body).

fields.label: Do
fields.html:
• push the motor into the nacelle bore (crush ribs; scrape a rib if it's too tight);
  • fit the body onto the nacelle plate and drive the 4 motor screws and 2 nacelle screws from inside the guard;
  • cut the motor leads to about 55 and solder them to the three 16 AWG extensions, joints staggered along the journal bore, each under 4.8 mm heat-shrink;
  • thread the leads out through the hollow journal.

fields.label: Check
fields.html: the motor-screw heads sit below the wheel's web plane with daylight. This was 0 mm on attempt 3; the brief now asks for at least 1.5 to anything rotating.

steps.check: the motor-screw heads sit below the wheel's web plane with daylight. This was 0 mm on attempt 3; the brief now asks for at least 1.5 to anything rotating.

steps.title: Free the pod and set it on the 45 deg prop (new after review 7)
notes: TOOL_tilt45_prop is a printed tool, not a design part: its placed mesh comes from the scratch blend tools/tilt45_prop.py --blend writes (the one the step renders used). The post cover and its 4 screws are hidden and the tilt servo, horn and adapter are shifted +X 10, as in the step render.

fasteners.text: remove the 4 x M3 x 14 from the post cover.
fasteners.spec: remove the 4 x M3 x 14 from the post cover.

fastener_check.text: removes the 4 x M3 x 14 post-cover screws from step 8

fields.label: Why
fields.html: the tilt servo can't be powered yet: its lead isn't spliced and the battery goes in at step 14. Forcing the pod round would back-drive the servo's gears.

fields.label: Do
fields.html:
1. Take the right post cover off (+X).
  2. Slide the tilt servo, horn and adapter out +X about 10 mm. The hex key leaves its socket after 6.5. Don't turn the servo output while it's out.
  3. The pod swings free; unpowered it falls nose-down to the -3 stop. Lift the nose to the +46 stop and slide the prop in on the turntable from the front: the tall pad under the nip cover, the low foot along the turntable to the right post's front face.
  4. Let the pod settle onto the pad.

fields.label: Check
fields.html:
• the pod sits steady at 45 with your hands off;
  • the pad bears on the nip cover's flat underside, not on the thumbwheel (8.5 clear), so the gap setting is untouched;
  • the prop is 8.5 from where the cap goes. Measured in a scratch model with the prop added: 6/6 cap screws take a straight bit at 14 with it in place.

steps.check: - the pod sits steady at 45 with your hands off; - the pad bears on the nip cover's flat underside, not on the thumbwheel (8.5 clear), so the gap setting is untouched; - the prop is 8.5 from where the cap goes. Measured in a scratch model with the prop added: 6/6 cap screws take a straight bit at 14 with it in place.

warnings.text: The tilt servo can't be powered yet. Don't force the pod round: that back-drives the servo's gears. Free it by sliding the servo out instead.
Don't turn the servo output while it's out, or the key won't go back in at the same flat.
The prop's pad must bear on the nip cover's flat underside, not the thumbwheel (8.5 clear), so the gap setting is untouched.

fasteners.text: 6 x M3 x 10 countersunk ST (groove cap).

fields.label: Do
fields.html:
1. Pod at 45 on the prop.
  2. Lay the tilt and feeder bus leads and the launcher bundle in the turntable groove, down to the hub bore.
  3. Pull the pan lead up the hub bore until about 60 stands above the turntable; the 350 lead has 57.9 spare over its route. Bring the tilt and feeder ends to it.
  4. Cut the three plugs off.
    • Trim the tilt and feeder leads to route + 70: hold each end at the bore centre at turntable-top level and cut it 70 beyond that point. That is about 23 off the tilt lead and 110 off the feeder lead.
    • Leave the pan lead long.
    • Strip the leads and solder like wires 3-to-1 (V+ to V+, GND to GND, signal to signal), with card or foil round the bore to shield the PLA.
    • Heat-shrink each joint (4.8 mm), then the three together (12.7 mm).
    • The finished splice must be Ø10 x 20 or smaller.
  5. Lower the splice into the hub bore on the side away from the launcher bundle (az 35, toward front-right), bottom at the seat (z 74). It passes the hub gear with 1.0.
  6. Tie it to the bundle sleeve with a small cable tie so it turns with the turntable.
  7. Push the spare pan lead back down into its U-loop.
  8. Dress the service loops:
    • the tilt lead's spare as a flat S-fold in the groove between the hub and the right post (x 10..60; only the tilt lead runs there);
    • the feeder lead's spare pushed back up the left-post channel beside the bundle.
  9. Check the bundle hand-over (A6-02). Its moving end swings 5.66 side to side over ±90 pan, so leave the sleeve loose there (no tie). Turn the turntable slowly to both pan stops and watch through the bore: nothing pulls tight.
  10. Fit the groove cap over the posts (0.2 to the left post going down) and drive its 6 screws with a straight bit.

fields.label: Check
fields.html:
• the cap sits flat with no lead pinched under it. With a 20 splice there is 8 between the splice top and the cap, room for the leads to turn down (../renders/attempt-7/review/r02_sec_y4.02_splice_top_under_groove_cap.png shows the tight 25 case);
  • the splice can't climb out of the bore (the cap stops it).

steps.check: - the cap sits flat with no lead pinched under it. With a 20 splice there is 8 between the splice top and the cap, room for the leads to turn down (`../renders/attempt-7/review/r02_sec_y4.02_splice_top_under_groove_cap.png` shows the tight 25 case); - the splice can't climb out of the bore (the cap stops it).

warnings.text: The finished splice must be Ø10 x 20 or smaller.
Shield the PLA round the bore with card or foil while soldering.
Leave the bundle sleeve loose at the hand-over (no tie): it swings 5.66 over ±90 pan.

fields.label: Do
fields.html:
1. Lift the pod nose to +46 and take the prop out. Lower the pod to the -3 stop.
  2. Slide the tilt servo back -X until its hex key re-enters the journal-plate socket. Rock the pod a degree to line up the flats.
  3. Refit the post cover.

fields.label: Check
fields.html: the pod has no free play at the key. Keep the prop: it's also the service fixture for the splice.

assembly_order.step: 12 jar on the bench: adapter in the band, gate laid closed on the valve floor (stop lug up), valve onto the spout (the spout tip captures the lug; v2-A1-09); v2-A2-A1-09 detent clip screwed on the +Y cheek, bump dropped into the closed notch

fasteners.text: 3 x M3 x 10 socket cap ST (valve, radial)
fasteners.spec: M3 x 10 socket cap ST (valve, radial)

fields.label: Do
fields.html:
• put the printed adapter disc into the band in place of the flat lid;
  • lay the gate on the valve's gate floor, closed, stop lug up at the -X end;
  • fit the valve over the spout with its 3 radial screws. The gate is captive from now on;
  • hold the detent clip's tab on the +Y cheek, gate closed, so the bump drops into the closed notch. Drive the self-tapper -Y until its head is flush in the counterbore.

fields.label: Check

  2. Screw on the adapter and band.

steps.title: First power-up (bench, wheel not spinning)

fields.label: Do
fields.html:
1. Power up with the flywheel motor disabled.
  2. Ping each servo by ID.
  3. Command tilt 0 and check the pod is level. If it isn't, set a tilt offset in firmware rather than moving the horn. After 11a.0 the key went back in at the same flat only if the servo wasn't turned.
  4. Command pan 0 (pod facing +Y) and the feeder to park (solid disc over the outlet), and trim any offsets.
  5. Clamp firmware tilt to 0..45; the printed stops are at -3 / +46.
  6. Only then spin up the flywheel.

fields.label: Check
fields.html:
• one fire command (disc +60, back to 0) drops exactly one candy, and the next shot uses -60;
  • log the leaf preload on day 0 (BOM section 0, "Leaf creep").

steps.check: - one fire command (disc +60, back to 0) drops exactly one candy, and the next shot uses -60; - log the leaf preload on day 0 (BOM section 0, "Leaf creep").

warnings.text: Power up with the flywheel motor disabled. Spin it up only after the servos are pinged, trimmed and the tilt is clamped to 0..45 in firmware.
If the pod isn't level at tilt 0, set a firmware offset rather than moving the horn.
